items.title: CVE-2026-105192 — LMCache: Remote code execution via unsafe deserialization in multiprocess mode transport
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-105192 affectant lmcache (pip) (score CVSS 9.8).

LMCache: Remote code execution via unsafe deserialization in multiprocess mode transport

LMCache multiprocess mode, also called distributed mode, opens an unauthenticated ZeroMQ ROUTER so worker processes can register and share KV cache blocks. The intended clients are sibling LMCache processes. There is no CURVE, ZAP, password, or message authentication on that socket. LMCache used only inside a vLLM process does not open this port.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-105192 affectant lmcache (pip) (score CVSS 9.8).

LMCache: Remote code execution via unsafe deserialization in multiprocess mode transport

LMCache multiprocess mode, also called distributed mode, opens an unauthenticated ZeroMQ ROUTER so worker processes can register and share KV cache blocks. The intended clients are sibling LMCache processes. There is no CURVE, ZAP, password, or message authentication on that socket. LMCache used only inside a vLLM process does not open this port. The transport binds to localhost unless the operator sets a routable address with --host, which is how multi-node deployments let peers connect. The 9.8 score is for that routable configuration. A stock single-host install that leaves the default bind is not reachable from other machines.

Messages on the socket are msgpack. Extension code 1 is registered for DeviceIPCWrapper and is passed to DeviceIPCWrapper.Deserialize in lmcache/v1/platform/base/ipc_wrapper.py, which calls pickle.loads. That hook runs from ext_hook in lmcache/v1/multiprocess/custom_types.py while the server is still decoding REGISTER_KV_CACHE arguments, before the handler runs. A single unauthenticated ZMQ DEALER message to the transport port (default 5555) therefore executes code as the user the LMCache process runs as. Official container images run that process as root.

The decode path shipped in v0.3.9. It is still present in the latest PyPI release, v0.5.5, in the v0.5.6 release candidates through v0.5.6rc3, and on the dev branch as of 2026-10-07. No fixed version has been published.

This is the documented multi-node setting. The ZMQ transport listens on port 5555.

python -m lmcache.v1.multiprocess.http_server \ --http-host 127.0.0.1 --http-port 8080 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5555 \ -

The suspected PRC-aligned group Armory Castle has been observed exploiting the newly disclosed flaw for long-term persistence

A suspected China state-sponsored actor has exploited a newly disclosed critical vulnerability in a BeyondTrust Remote Support instance, Google has warned.

The threat actor, tracked as Armory Castle, was observed to escalate privileges and established persistent access to compromised BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances following exploitation of the flaw, CVE-2026-102764, in August 2026.

BeyondTrust publicly disclosed the vulnerability, which has a CVSS rating of 9.3, on October 15.

A patch was released on October 8 for software-as-a-service (SaaS) and self-hosted customers. The vendor said it is withholding technical details of the vulnerability, as disclosing such information while appliances are still being patched could put customers at an increased risk.

In its blog published on October 15, Google urged affected BeyondTrust customers to apply patches immediately.

“Organizations should prepare for potential widespread exploitation following this disclosure, as Armory Castle and other threat actors have historically conducted broad, opportunistic exploitation once the vulnerability becomes public,” the tech giant wrote.

items.title: CVE-2026-96627 — Arcane: Delegated users:update permission allows admin account takeover via password reset (no privilege-hierarchy check)
items.body:
Vulnérabilité élevée CVE-2026-96627 affectant github.com/getarcaneapp/arcane/backend/v2 (go) (score CVSS 8.8).

Arcane: Delegated users:update permission allows admin account takeover via password reset (no privilege-hierarchy check)

UpdateUser (handler backend/api/handlers/users.go:317-323 ) loads the target by ID and sets userModel.PasswordHash from the request body for any user, then userService.UpdateUser ( user_service.go:174 ) simply tx.Save s — with NO actor-vs-target privilege comparison.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité élevée CVE-2026-96627 affectant github.com/getarcaneapp/arcane/backend/v2 (go) (score CVSS 8.8).

Arcane: Delegated users:update permission allows admin account takeover via password reset (no privilege-hierarchy check)

UpdateUser (handler backend/api/handlers/users.go:317-323 ) loads the target by ID and sets userModel.PasswordHash from the request body for any user, then userService.UpdateUser ( user_service.go:174 ) simply tx.Save s — with NO actor-vs-target privilege comparison. The only IsGlobalAdmin guard ( user_service.go:345 ) is a last-admin check inside DeleteUser , not the update path. Role assignment / role CRUD are RequireGlobalAdmin ( backend/pkg/authz/permissions.go:27-33 ), proving users:update is intended below admin.

Complete administrator account takeover (C:H/I:H/A:H) by any holder of the delegated users:update permission.

items.title: lopdf has a stack overflow via deeply nested PDF objects
items.body:
Vulnérabilité élevée affectant lopdf (rust) (score CVSS 7.5).

lopdf has a stack overflow via deeply nested PDF objects

Because this is a stack-overflow abort rather than a panic! , it cannot be caught with catch_unwind : any service that parses untrusted PDF input with lopdf can be crashed by a ~21 KB file, resulting in a denial of service.

Confirmed on lopdf 0.41.0 and earlier; fixed in 0.42.0.

En observant la syntaxe habituelle des courriels de cette société, par exemple prenom.nom@entreprise.fr , il devient un jeu d’enfant de déduire son adresse directe, même si celle-ci n’a jamais été publiée explicitement sur Internet. Pourtant, comme le souligne la CNIL (Commission Nationale de l’Informatique et des Libertés), le fait qu’une information soit accessible en ligne ne signifie pas qu’elle soit librement exploitable . Reconstituer une adresse électronique professionnelle constitue un traitement de données personnelles à part entière, soumis à des règles strictes. Entre intérêt légitime et respect de la vie privée Pour justifier cette pratique sans avoir à demander un accord préalable, les organismes s’appuient généralement sur la notion d’« intérêt légitime » prévue par le RGPD . Mais la CNIL avertit que ce fondement juridique n’est pas un chèque en blanc. L’entreprise doit impérativement prouver que son besoin de contact est réel et qu’il ne porte pas une atteinte excessive aux droits de l’interlocuteur. Toute la question repose sur ce que le professionnel peut « raisonnablement s’attendre »

Officials in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, confirmed that hackers stole files from government systems during an incident in August.

A county spokesperson told Recorded Future News that they discovered “irregular activity” on August 28 and began an investigation on a “limited subset of systems within the county computer network.”

“Through the course of the county’s response and investigation, it was determined that an unauthorized actor gained access to a limited number of systems and copied certain files from those systems,” the spokesperson said.

The spokesperson did not respond to questions about what data was involved but said investigators are currently reviewing the files to determine whether any stolen information related to residents of the county.

The Baltimore suburb is home to more than 600,000 residents and the state’s capital of Annapolis. Washington, D.C. is nearby, as well. Dozens of federal agencies have offices or headquarters in the county, including the Defense Department, the Internal Revenue Service, the Environmental Protection Agency, the Social Security Administration, the Department of Agriculture, the U.S. Coast Guard and more.

County officials said they notified federal law enforcement about the data breach as well as other government agencies.

Cybersecurity giant Proofpoint says it will acquire Miami-based data visibility and security company Varonis in an all-cash transaction worth $6.3 billion.

“The combined company will serve more than 16,000 enterprises and millions of organizations globally, creating one of the world’s leading pure-play cybersecurity companies and establishing the industry's largest data and AI cybersecurity organization,” Proofpoint said in announcing the deal on Thursday.

Miami-based Varonis, founded in 2005, focuses on data visibility and security. The footprint for California-headquartered Proofpoint, founded in 2002, traditionally includes email security and identity threat defense. It’s owned by private equity firm Thoma Bravo.

AI figured prominently in Thursday’s announcement. The goal is to create a platform that “helps organizations adopt AI with confidence: finding and protecting sensitive data, controlling what people and AI can access, and stopping data loss.”

Varonis researchers recently got headlines for a report in which they manipulated Microsoft’s AI assistant Copilot Personal into explaining how to hack itself.

Proofpoint analysts published research earlier this month about a high-level, apparently China-backed phishing campaign geared toward espionage.

Signal de veille — The Register.

The October 2026 Windows security update may break networking for some customers who are still clinging to long-deprecated NTLMv1 security. A seemingly minor change in the update could have major implications for administrators and enterprises that haven't fully moved away from the legacy technology. Before the October 2026 update, Windows permitted NTLMv1-derived credentials for Single Sign-On and generated warning events. After the update, requests to use NTLMv1-derived credentials are blocked. It comes down to the BlockNtlmSSO registry value. If it hasn't been set, Windows will now use Enforce mode (1) instead of Audit mode (0), thus blocking requests and potentially impacting Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and VPN authentication, and therefore connections. The update does not set the value of BlockNtlmSSO, and administrators can set it to 0 to temporarily allow NTLMv1-derived Single Sign-On credentials. However, Microsoft noted, "Using Audit mode reduces the protection provided by Enforce mode and should only be considered as a scoped, temporary security exception." To be clear, this is not a bug and is by design. The addition of NTLM to the deprecation list occurred in 2024, and Microsoft added audit logs for NTLMv1 usage in late August 2025.
